words.en: A veil is a piece of thin soft cloth that women sometimes wear over their heads and which can also cover their face.

words.tr:
v. 呻吟；叹息
n. 呻吟声；叹息声
words.ex: He groaned when he saw the heavy box.
words.ex_cn: 他看到那个沉重的箱子时呻吟了一声。
words.en: If you groan, you make a long, low sound because you are in pain, or because you are upset or unhappy about something.

words.ex: They tease him because he wears funny hats.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他戴滑稽的帽子而戏弄他。
words.en: To tease someone means to make fun of them or try to provoke them in a playful way.

words.ex: They discriminate against people because of their race.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为种族而歧视他人。
words.en: To discriminate means to recognize a distinction; differentiate. It can also mean to make an unjust or prejudicial distinction in the treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, sex, or age.

words.ex: The new law will supersede the old one.
words.ex_cn: 新法律将取代旧法律。
words.en: If something is superseded by something newer, it is replaced because it has become old-fashioned or unacceptable.

words.tr: n. 代理；副职；恶习；缺点；
words.ex: He acted as vice for the manager during her absence.
words.ex_cn: 在经理缺席期间，他担任代理。
words.en: A vice is a moral fault or weakness in someone's character.

words.tr:
n. （赶牲畜的）尖头棒；激励；刺激
v. 刺激；驱使
words.ex: The farmer used a goad to guide the oxen.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用一根尖头棒赶牛。
words.en: If you goad someone, you deliberately make them feel angry or irritated, often causing them to react by doing something.

words.tr: adj. 脱离正道的；脱离常轨的
words.ex: His aberrant behavior surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他反常的行为让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: An aberrant person or thing is one that is unusual or unexpected, especially in an unwelcome way.

words.ex: The hospital is a public institution.
words.ex_cn: 这家医院是一家公共机构。
words.en: An institution is a large important organization such as a university, church, or bank.

words.tr: adj. 陡峭的；急剧升降的；
words.ex: The mountain has a steep path.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有一条陡峭的小路。
words.en: A steep slope or hill is one that is at a sharp angle, rather than being flat or gradual.

words.tr: adj. 根深蒂固的；积习难改的
words.ex: He is an inveterate smoker who cannot quit.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个根深蒂固的吸烟者，无法戒掉。
words.en: If you describe someone as, for example, an inveterate liar or smoker, you mean that they have lied or smoked for a long time and are not likely to stop doing it.

words.ex: The inexorable flow of time cannot be stopped.
words.ex_cn: 时间不可阻挡地流逝。
words.en: If you describe something as inexorable, you mean that it is impossible to stop or prevent from happening.

words.ex: He posits that the earth is round.
words.ex_cn: 他提出地球是圆的。
words.en: To posit something is to suggest it as a basic fact or principle from which a further idea is formed or developed.

words.ex: The temple is a divine place.
words.ex_cn: 这座寺庙是神的圣地。
words.en: Something that is divine relates to a god or goddess.

words.tr: v. 使迷失方向；使迷惘
words.ex: The storm disoriented the hikers.
words.ex_cn: 风暴使徒步者迷失了方向。
words.en: To cause someone to lose their sense of direction or to become confused.

words.tr: v. 使迷惑；使...不知所措
words.ex: The strange signs bewilder the children.
words.ex_cn: 这些奇怪的符号让孩子们感到迷惑。
words.en: If something bewilders you, it is so confusing or difficult that you cannot understand it.

words.ex: It is customary to shake hands when you meet someone.
words.ex_cn: 见面时握手是习惯做法。
words.en: Something that is customary is normal because it is the way something is usually done.

words.ex: His tall height is hereditary from his parents.
words.ex_cn: 他高高的身材是遗传自父母的。
words.en: A hereditary characteristic or illness is passed from the genes of a parent to a child.

words.ex: The latent talent in the child became clear after years of practice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子潜在的才能在多年练习后显现出来。
words.en: Latent is used to describe something which is hidden and not obvious at the moment, but which may develop further in the future.

words.ex: The police investigated the assault on the old man.
words.ex_cn: 警方调查了对那位老人的攻击。
words.en: An assault is a physical attack on someone, or a military attack on a place.

words.ex: He steers the team toward success.
words.ex_cn: 他引导团队走向成功。
words.en: To steer a vehicle, ship, or aircraft is to control its direction.

words.ex: The company will consolidate two departments next month.
words.ex_cn: 公司下个月将合并两个部门。
words.en: To consolidate something means to make it stronger, more secure, or more solid.

words.tr: adj. 有骑士风度的；彬彬有礼的；侠义的
words.ex: The knight was chivalrous and helped the lady.
words.ex_cn: 这位骑士有骑士精神，帮助了那位女士。
words.en: A chivalrous man is polite, kind, and unselfish, especially towards women.

words.ex: The school used to segregate students by race.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校过去按种族隔离学生。
words.en: To segregate means to separate one group of people, animals, or things from another, especially because they are of different types or belong to different categories.

words.tr: adj. 原始的；远古的；最初的
words.ex: The primordial soup formed the first life on Earth.
words.ex_cn: 原始汤形成了地球上的最初生命。
words.en: Primordial means existing at or from the beginning of time; primeval.

words.ex: I saw an advert on TV for new shoes.
words.ex_cn: 我在电视上看到一双新鞋的广告。
words.en: An advert is a notice or announcement in a public medium promoting a product, service, or event.

words.tr: adj. 虚拟的；几乎的；实际上的；事实上的；
words.ex: He played a virtual game on his computer.
words.ex_cn: 他在电脑上玩了一个虚拟游戏。
words.en: If you describe something as virtual, you mean that it is so nearly true that for most purposes it can be regarded as true.

words.ex: The animals found refuge in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这些动物在森林中找到了避难所。
words.en: A place or state of safety or shelter from danger, trouble, or difficulty.

words.ex: He will delineate the plan clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他将清晰地描述这个计划。
words.en: To delineate something means to describe or portray it precisely.

words.tr: adj. 明目张胆的；公然的；喧闹的
words.ex: He made a blatant lie to avoid punishment.
words.ex_cn: 他为了逃避惩罚，公然撒了谎。
words.en: If you describe an action as blatant, you mean that it is done in an open and obvious way, often with a lack of shame or embarrassment.

words.tr: adj. 明白易懂的；表达清楚的
words.ex: The instructions were written in a perspicuous manner.
words.ex_cn: 说明书写得清晰易懂。
words.en: If you describe something such as an argument or explanation as perspicuous, you mean that it is clear and easy to understand.

words.ex: The subtlety of her smile made everyone curious.
words.ex_cn: 她微笑的微妙之处让所有人都感到好奇。
words.en: The quality of being subtle, especially in a way that is difficult to notice or understand.

words.tr:
adj. 首要的；大红色的
n. 红衣主教；枢机主教；基数
words.ex: This is a cardinal rule in our school.
words.ex_cn: 这是我们学校的一项首要规则。
words.en: A cardinal rule or quality is the most important one.

words.ex: They plant trees to commemorate the fallen soldiers.
words.ex_cn: 他们种树以纪念阵亡的士兵。
words.en: To commemorate an important event or person means to remember them by means of a special action, ceremony, or specially created object.

words.ex: The book has a gloss at the bottom of each page.
words.ex_cn: 这本书每页底部都有注释。
words.en: A gloss is a bright shine on the surface of something. It can also refer to a superficial appearance or interpretation that conceals the true nature of something.

words.ex: He won't divulge the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他不会泄露这个秘密。
words.en: If you divulge a piece of secret or private information, you tell it to someone.

words.ex: The car has a sleek design.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车有着流畅的外形。
words.en: Sleek describes something that is smooth, glossy, and streamlined, often implying a sense of elegance and efficiency.

words.ex: The buoyancy of the water helps the boat float.
words.ex_cn: 水的浮力帮助船漂浮。
words.en: Buoyancy is the ability of something to float in a liquid or to rise in air or gas.

words.ex: He is an eccentric man who wears socks with sandals.
words.ex_cn: 他是个古怪的人，穿着袜子配凉鞋。
words.en: If you say that someone is eccentric, you mean that they behave in a strange way, and have habits or opinions that are different from those of most people.

words.tr: n. 肤色；面色；情况；局面
words.ex: Her complexion is very fair.
words.ex_cn: 她的肤色非常白皙。
words.en: The natural color, texture, and appearance of a person's skin, especially of the face.

words.tr: adj. 熙熙攘攘的； v. “bustle”的现在分词；
words.ex: The market is bustling with people.
words.ex_cn: 市场里人来人往，熙熙攘攘。
words.en: If a place is bustling, it is full of busy activity.

words.ex: He tries to attune his ears to the quiet sound.
words.ex_cn: 他试图让自己的耳朵适应那细微的声音。
words.en: If you attune your ear or your senses to something, you become used to it and can recognize it or understand it.

words.ex: She showed great affection for her little dog.
words.ex_cn: 她对她的小狗非常钟爱。
words.en: A feeling of liking and caring for someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 卑屈的；恭顺的；次要的；从属的
words.ex: He is subservient to his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他对他的老板唯命是从。
words.en: If you are subservient, you do whatever someone wants you to do.

words.ex: He surmounted his fears to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 他克服了恐惧，在公众面前发言。
words.en: If you surmount a problem or difficulty, you deal successfully with it.

words.tr: adj. 感官的；肉欲的；愉悦感官的；耽于肉欲的
words.ex: The sensual smell of fresh bread made her hungry.
words.ex_cn: 新鲜面包的感官香味让她感到饥饿。
words.en: Relating to or involving gratification of the senses and physical, especially sexual, pleasure.

words.ex: The government made a fiscal decision to lower taxes.
words.ex_cn: 政府做出了降低税收的财政决定。
words.en: Fiscal is used to describe something that relates to government money or public money, especially taxes.

words.ex: One apple will suffice for now.
words.ex_cn: 一个苹果现在就足够了。
words.en: If something suffices, it is enough to achieve a purpose or to fulfill a need.

words.tr:
n. （古罗马的）贵族；名门望族；有教养的人；罗马帝国的地方官
adj. 贵族的；贵族似的；上流社会的
words.ex: She was born into a patrician family.
words.ex_cn: 她出生在一个贵族家庭。
words.en: A patrician is a person of high birth or noble status, especially in ancient Rome.

words.ex: He amended the letter before sending it.
words.ex_cn: 他在发送信件之前修正了它。
words.en: To amend something means to make changes to it in order to improve it or make it more accurate.

words.ex: He spoke quietly lest he wake the baby.
words.ex_cn: 他低声说话，以免吵醒婴儿。
words.en: If you do something lest something unpleasant should happen, you do it to try to prevent the unpleasant thing from happening.

words.ex: The two clocks synchronize automatically.
words.ex_cn: 这两座钟自动同时发生。
words.en: If you synchronize two activities, processes, or movements, or if you synchronize one activity, process, or movement with another, you cause them to happen at the same time and speed as each other.

words.tr: adj. 令人安心的； v. “reassure”的现在分词；
words.ex: Her smile was reassuring.
words.ex_cn: 她的微笑令人安心。
words.en: If you find someone's words or actions reassuring, they make you feel less worried about something.

words.ex: The weather can dictate what we wear each day.
words.ex_cn: 天气可以支配我们每天穿什么。
words.en: To dictate means to say or read something aloud for someone else to write down, or to give orders in an authoritative manner.

words.ex: The synonym of 'happy' is 'glad'.
words.ex_cn: ‘happy’的同义词是‘glad’。
words.en: A synonym is a word or phrase that means exactly or nearly the same as another word or phrase in the same language.

words.ex: Hitherto, no one has solved the problem.
words.ex_cn: 迄今为止，没有人解决过这个问题。
words.en: Until now or until the point in time under discussion.

words.tr: n. 影响；方位；轴承；举止； v. 忍受；“bear”的现在分词；
words.ex: The new policy has a big bearing on our daily lives.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策对我们日常生活有很大影响。
words.en: The manner in which one conducts or carries oneself, including posture and gestures; also refers to a machine part that supports another part and reduces friction.

words.tr: adj. 深远的；影响深远的
words.ex: The decision had far-reaching effects on the town.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定对这个城镇产生了深远的影响。
words.en: If you describe actions, events, or changes as far-reaching, you mean that they have a very great influence and affect a great number of things.

words.tr: adj. 轻松愉快的；无忧无虑的；随便的；漫不经心的
words.ex: He gave a lighthearted laugh during the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上开心地笑了。
words.en: If someone is lighthearted, they are cheerful and happy.

words.ex: He tried to extenuate his mistake by saying he was tired.
words.ex_cn: 他试图以自己累了为由减轻自己的错误。
words.en: To lessen or to try to lessen the seriousness or extent of (guilt or an offense) by providing partial excuses.

words.ex: He expressed dissent about the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 他对新规定提出了异议。
words.en: Dissent is strong disagreement or dissatisfaction with a decision or opinion, especially one that is supported by most people or by people in authority.

words.tr: adj. 有独创性的；巧妙的；
words.ex: The child came up with an ingenious way to solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子想出了一个有独创性的方式来解决这个谜题。
words.en: Something that is ingenious is very clever and involves new ideas, methods, or equipment.

words.ex: The soldier wore camouflage to hide in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 士兵穿着伪装服在森林中隐藏自己。
words.en: Camouflage is the way in which some animals are colored and shaped so that they cannot easily be seen in their natural surroundings.

words.ex: Her mornings are hectic with work and kids.
words.ex_cn: 她的早晨因为工作和孩子而紧张忙碌。
words.en: If you describe a situation as hectic, you mean that it is very busy and involves a lot of rushed activity.

words.ex: The refugees lived in abject poverty.
words.ex_cn: 这些难民过着凄惨的贫困生活。
words.en: Abject means extremely bad, unpleasant, and degrading.

words.tr: adj. 无望的；凄凉的；荒凉的；
words.ex: The future looks bleak without a job.
words.ex_cn: 没有工作，未来看起来毫无希望。
words.en: If you describe a situation as bleak, you mean that it seems unlikely to improve or get better.

words.ex: The case will be heard in court next week.
words.ex_cn: 这个案件将于下周在法院审理。
words.en: A court is a place where legal matters are decided by a judge and jury or by a magistrate.

words.ex: He is an avid reader of mystery novels.
words.ex_cn: 他热衷于阅读侦探小说。
words.en: If you say that someone is avid for something, you mean that they are very eager to get it.

words.tr: v. 兜售；招徕；吹捧；倒卖（高价票）
words.ex: He touts the new phone as the best on the market.
words.ex_cn: 他吹捧这款新手机是市场上最好的。
words.en: If someone touts something, they try to sell it or convince people that it is good, especially in an aggressive or exaggerated way.

words.ex: Love is an intangible thing.
words.ex_cn: 爱是一种无形的东西。
words.en: Something that is intangible is not able to be touched or seen, but is still important or valuable.

words.tr: adj. 吹毛求疵的；挑剔的
words.ex: He made a captious comment about the small mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他对一个小错误发表了挑剔的评论。
words.en: Tending to find fault or raise petty objections.

words.tr: n. (尤指道德方面的)戒律；准则
words.ex: He follows the precept to be kind every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天遵循要善良的教诲。
words.en: A precept is a general rule intended to regulate behavior or thought.

words.tr:
n. 幼鹿；浅黄褐色
v. 奉承；讨好
words.ex: The forest was filled with the sounds of baby fawns.
words.ex_cn: 森林里充满了幼鹿的叫声。
words.en: If someone fawns over you, they flatter you and show you too much attention.

words.ex: She wore a dress for the occasion.
words.ex_cn: 她为了这个特殊场合穿了一条裙子。
words.en: An occasion is a particular time when something happens, or a special event.

words.tr:
v. 耗尽；用完；使筋疲力尽
n. 排气管；废气
words.ex: The long hike exhausted him.
words.ex_cn: 这次漫长的徒步旅行让他筋疲力尽。
words.en: If something exhausts you, it makes you so tired, either physically or mentally, that you have no energy left.

words.ex: The team was relegated to the second division after losing all their games.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍在输掉所有比赛后被降级到第二级别联赛。
words.en: If you relegate someone or something to a less important position, you give them this position.

words.tr: n. （宗教等的）仪式；例行习惯；
words.ex: The village holds a ritual every spring to pray for good weather.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄每年春天都举行一个仪式，祈求好天气。
words.en: A ritual is a religious service or other ceremony which involves a series of actions performed in a fixed order.

words.ex: The confederacy fought against the union in the civil war.
words.ex_cn: 南方联盟在内战中与联邦作战。
words.en: A confederacy is a union of states or groups of people who have joined together for a common purpose or by a common agreement.

words.ex: They tried to subvert the government.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图颠覆政府。
words.en: To subvert means to undermine the power and authority of an established system or institution.

words.tr: adj. 庸俗的；粗俗的；粗野的；下流的
words.ex: He used a vulgar word in class.
words.ex_cn: 他在课堂上说了一个粗俗的词。
words.en: If you describe something as vulgar, you mean that it is in bad taste or of poor quality.

words.tr: adj. 清醒的；严肃的；素淡的；
words.ex: He stayed sober after drinking only water.
words.ex_cn: 他只喝了水，保持清醒。
words.en: If you are sober, you are not drunk. If you are sober, you are serious and thoughtful.

words.tr:
adj. 本国的；地方的
n. 方言；土语
words.ex: He wrote the poem in the vernacular language.
words.ex_cn: 他用本国语言写了这首诗。
words.en: The vernacular is the language or dialect spoken by the ordinary people in a particular country or region.

words.ex: They persecute people for their beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他们因人们的信仰而迫害他们。
words.en: If someone is persecuted, they are treated cruelly and unfairly, often because of their race, religion, or political beliefs.

words.ex: He is literally the best player on the team.
words.ex_cn: 他确实是队里最好的球员。
words.en: In a literal manner or sense; exactly.

words.ex: People congregate in the park on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 人们在周末聚集在公园里。
words.en: To congregate means to come together in a group or crowd.

words.ex: The court will prosecute him for theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院将因盗窃罪起诉他。
words.en: To prosecute means to institute legal proceedings against someone or to carry on a legal action against a defendant in a court of law. It also means to continue with or carry on an activity or enterprise.

words.ex: We sit together and reminisce about old times.
words.ex_cn: 我们坐在一起回忆过去的时光。
words.en: If you reminisce about something from your past, you write or talk about it, often with pleasure.

words.ex: The pendulum oscillate slowly.
words.ex_cn: 钟摆缓慢地摆动。
words.en: If an object oscillates, it moves repeatedly from one position to another and back again, or if a figure or value oscillates, it keeps moving up and down.

words.ex: He commiserated with his friend after the loss.
words.ex_cn: 他在朋友失利后安慰了他。
words.en: If you commiserate with someone, you show them pity or sympathy because something unpleasant has happened to them.

words.ex: He is prone to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If you are prone to a particular problem or characteristic, you are likely to be affected by it or to have it.

words.tr: adj. 虔诚的；信神的；伪善的
words.ex: He is a pious man who prays every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个每天祈祷的虔诚的人。
words.en: Someone who is pious is very religious and moral.

words.ex: The doctor gave him a clinical exam.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他做了临床检查。
words.en: Clinical means involving or relating to the direct observation and treatment of patients, rather than theoretical or laboratory studies.

words.ex: The satellite beams signals to Earth.
words.ex_cn: 卫星向地球发射信号。
words.en: A beam is a long, thick piece of wood, metal, or concrete that is used to support the roof of a building. It can also refer to a line of light that shines from a bright object, or a smile that shows someone is very happy.

words.tr: adj. 鲁莽的；不计后果的；
words.ex: He drove reckless and got into an accident.
words.ex_cn: 他开车鲁莽，结果出了事故。
words.en: If you say that someone is reckless, you mean that they act in a way which shows that they do not care about danger or the effect their behaviour will have on other people.

words.tr:
v. 皱眉；蹙额
n. 皱眉；蹙额
words.ex: He frowns when he hears bad news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到坏消息时会皱眉。
words.en: If you frown, you bring your eyebrows together so that there are lines on your face above your eyes, often because you are annoyed or worried.

words.ex: His countenance showed surprise.
words.ex_cn: 他的面容流露出惊讶。
words.en: A person's face or facial expression; support or approval.

words.ex: The remnant of the old wall still stands.
words.ex_cn: 这堵旧墙的残余部分仍然矗立着。
words.en: A remnant is a small remaining quantity of something.

words.tr: n. 投票；选举权；参政权
words.ex: Women won suffrage in 1920.
words.ex_cn: 女性在1920年获得了选举权。
words.en: Suffrage is the right to vote in political elections.

words.tr:
n. 首次露面；初次登场
v. 初次登场；首次推出
words.ex: He made his debut on stage last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚在舞台上首次登台。
words.en: The debut of a performer or sports player is their first public performance, appearance, or recording.

words.ex: The class will commence at 9 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 课程将在上午9点开始。
words.en: To begin something; to start.

words.ex: She replenished the water bottle after the hike.
words.ex_cn: 她在徒步后补充了水瓶里的水。
words.en: If you replenish something, you make it full or complete again.

words.tr: adj. 吵闹的；喧哗的；吵吵嚷嚷的
words.ex: The clamorous crowd cheered loudly for the winner.
words.ex_cn: 喧闹的人群为获胜者大声欢呼。
words.en: If you describe people or their voices as clamorous, you mean they are talking loudly or shouting.

words.ex: She knit a warm scarf for her brother.
words.ex_cn: 她为她的弟弟织了一条暖和的围巾。
words.en: If you knit something, especially an article of clothing, you make it from wool or a similar thread by using two knitting needles or a machine.

words.ex: The plastic is pliable and easy to bend.
words.ex_cn: 这种塑料柔韧，容易弯曲。
words.en: A pliable object or material is easy to bend or shape without breaking.

words.ex: The painting has a simple aesthetic appeal.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有一种简单的审美吸引力。
words.en: Concerned with beauty or the appreciation of beauty.

words.tr: adj. 有...气味的；令人想起...的
words.ex: The garden is redolent of roses.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园弥漫着玫瑰的香气。
words.en: Strongly reminiscent or suggestive of something.

words.tr:
n. 禁止贸易令；禁运
v. 禁止…的贸易；禁运
words.ex: The country placed an embargo on imported goods.
words.ex_cn: 该国对进口商品实施了禁运。
words.en: An embargo is an official order to stop trade with another country.

words.ex: He is a paragon of honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他是诚实的典范。
words.en: A paragon is someone who is considered to be a perfect example of a particular quality.

words.tr:
n. 总计；集合体
adj. 合计的；总的
v. （使）聚集；聚合；总计为
words.ex: The aggregate of all sales this month is $50,000.
words.ex_cn: 本月所有销售额的总计是5万美元。
words.en: An aggregate is a number of things or people that are considered as a group or a whole.

words.tr:
n. 探测器；
v. 探查；
words.ex: The probe sent back photos from Mars.
words.ex_cn: 探测器从火星传回了照片。
words.en: If you probe into something, you ask questions or try to discover facts about it. A probe is also a long thin instrument that doctors and dentists use to examine parts of the body.

words.ex: This rule pertains to all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: If one thing pertains to another, it relates, belongs, or applies to it.

words.ex: He gave her flowers to placate her.
words.ex_cn: 他送她花来安抚她。
words.en: If you placate someone, you do or say something to make them stop feeling angry.

words.tr:
n. 骗局；恶作剧；戏弄
v. 愚弄
words.ex: The news was a hoax to scare people.
words.ex_cn: 这则新闻是个骗局，为了吓唬人。
words.en: A hoax is a plan to deceive someone, such as telling the police there is a bomb somewhere when there is not, or a trick in which someone tells people a lie.

words.ex: He devised a new way to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他设计了一种解决这个问题的新方法。
words.en: To devise something means to plan or invent a new way of doing something.

words.ex: His melodramatic crying made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他感情夸张的哭泣让大家都笑了。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as melodramatic, you are criticizing them for acting in a way that is too emotional or exaggerated.

words.ex: The insurrection failed because people did not support it.
words.ex_cn: 这次起义失败了，因为人们不支持它。
words.en: An insurrection is a violent uprising against an authority or government.

words.tr: n. 落伍者；掉队者；落在最后的人（或动物）
words.ex: The straggler arrived late to the group.
words.ex_cn: 那个落伍者迟到了，没跟上队伍。
words.en: A straggler is a person or thing that is late or slow in comparison with others in a group, often because they are moving more slowly or are less organized.

words.tr: n. 山崩；塌方；压倒性的胜利
words.ex: The heavy rain caused a landslide.
words.ex_cn: 大雨引发了山体滑坡。
words.en: A landslide is a victory in an election in which a person or political party gets far more votes or seats than their opponents.

words.tr: n. 停滞；滞止；萧条；迟钝
words.ex: The economy is in stagnation.
words.ex_cn: 经济处于停滞状态。
words.en: A situation in which there is no progress or development.

words.tr: adj. 暂定的；不确定的；试验性的；
words.ex: We made a tentative plan to meet next week.
words.ex_cn: 我们制定了一个下周见面的暂定计划。
words.en: If you make a tentative suggestion or plan, you make it without being sure that it is right or acceptable.

words.ex: He invoked the law to protect his rights.
words.ex_cn: 他援引法律来保护自己的权利。
words.en: If you invoke a law, rule, or principle, you refer to it as a reason or justification for something.

words.ex: Sugar dissolves in water.
words.ex_cn: 糖在水中溶解。
words.en: If a substance dissolves in liquid or if you dissolve a substance, it becomes mixed with the liquid and disappears.

words.ex: This movie is a horror genre film.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是一部恐怖类型影片。
words.en: A genre is a particular type of literature, painting, music, film, or other art form which people consider as a class because it has special characteristics.

words.ex: Sediments accrete on the ocean floor.
words.ex_cn: 沉积物在海底堆积。
words.en: To grow by accumulation or coalescence; to increase by external addition or growth.

words.ex: The feral cat lives in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 这只野生的猫生活在森林里。
words.en: A feral animal is a domestic animal that has returned to the wild, or is the offspring of such animals, and is not socialized to humans.

words.ex: The sailors cleaned the stern of the boat.
words.ex_cn: 水手们打扫了船尾。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behavior as stern, you mean that they are severe or strict.

words.ex: He surpassed his brother in math scores.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学成绩上超过了他弟弟。
words.en: If one person or thing surpasses another, the first is better than, or has more of a particular quality than, the second.

words.tr:
n. 彻底检修；大修；彻底革新；全面修订
v. 彻底检修；超过（赛跑对手）
words.ex: The plane needs an overhaul before the next flight.
words.ex_cn: 这架飞机在下次飞行前需要彻底检修。
words.en: If you overhaul a system or method, you examine it carefully and make many changes in it in order to improve it.

words.tr:
v. 缓慢而弯曲地流动；漫步；闲聊
n. 河流的曲折；漫步；迂回曲折的进程
words.ex: The river meanders through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这条河蜿蜒穿过森林。
words.en: To meander means to follow a winding and turning course, often used to describe the way a river flows or the way a person walks without a clear direction.

words.ex: The wizard conjure a fireball with ancient words.
words.ex_cn: 巫师用古老的咒语召唤出一个火球。
words.en: If you conjure something out of nothing, you make it appear as if by magic.

words.tr: n. 特性；怪癖；奇异之物
words.ex: One peculiarity of the old house is its red door.
words.ex_cn: 这座老房子的一个特点是它的红门。
words.en: A peculiarity is a characteristic or quality that is distinctive or unique to a particular person, place, or thing.

words.ex: She lamented the death of her dog.
words.ex_cn: 她哀悼她狗的去世。
words.en: If you lament something, you express your sadness, regret, or disappointment about it.

words.tr: adj. 观察力敏锐的；谨慎遵守的；
words.ex: She is observant and notices small details.
words.ex_cn: 她观察力敏锐，能注意到细小的细节。
words.en: Someone who is observant pays close attention to things and notices more about them than most people do.

words.tr:
adj. 热诚的；友好的
n. 甜露酒
words.ex: He gave a cordial smile to his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对着邻居露出了热情的微笑。
words.en: warm and friendly

words.tr:
v. 把…归因于；由…引起；
n. 品质；属性；特征；属性；
words.ex: He attributes his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you attribute something to an event or situation, you think that it was caused by that event or situation.

words.tr: adj. 残暴的；恶劣的；糟透的
words.ex: The dictator committed atrocious acts against his people.
words.ex_cn: 这位独裁者对人民犯下了残暴的罪行。
words.en: If you describe something as atrocious, you are emphasizing that its quality is very bad.

words.ex: He still feels rancor toward his old boss.
words.ex_cn: 他仍然对他的前老板怀有怨恨。
words.en: A feeling of deep and bitter anger and ill-will.

words.ex: The proximity of the school to the park makes it nice for kids.
words.ex_cn: 学校靠近公园，对孩子们来说很好。
words.en: Proximity refers to the state of being near in space or time.

words.tr:
adj. 唯利是图的；雇佣的
n. 雇佣兵；唯利是图者
words.ex: He works as a mercenary for money.
words.ex_cn: 他为了钱当雇佣兵。
words.en: A mercenary is a professional soldier hired to serve in a foreign army.

words.tr: n. 矛盾心理；正反感情并存
words.ex: He feels ambivalence about moving to a new city.
words.ex_cn: 他对搬到新城市感到矛盾。
words.en: Ambivalence is the state of having mixed feelings or contradictory attitudes about something or someone.

words.tr:
v. 使惊慌失措；使慌张
n. 慌张；慌乱
words.ex: He got flustered when the teacher asked him a question.
words.ex_cn: 当老师问他问题时，他变得慌乱了。
words.en: If you fluster someone, you make them feel nervous and confused by rushing them or by making it difficult for them to concentrate on what they are doing.

words.tr: v. 使焦虑；使不安；扰乱
words.ex: The noise perturbs the baby.
words.ex_cn: 噪音让婴儿不安。
words.en: If something perturbs you, it makes you feel anxious or worried.

words.tr: adj. 懒惰的；懒散的；好逸恶劳的
words.ex: He is indolent and never does his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他很懒，从不做作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as indolent, you mean that they are lazy.

words.ex: Interest will accrue over time.
words.ex_cn: 利息会随着时间积累。
words.en: If money or interest accrues, it gradually increases in amount over a period of time.

words.ex: He tried to seduce her with flowers and gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用鲜花和礼物引诱她。
words.en: To seduce someone means to persuade them to do something, especially something wrong or unwise, by making it seem attractive or exciting.

words.ex: He adduce evidence to prove his point.
words.ex_cn: 他提出证据来证明自己的观点。
words.en: To cite as evidence or proof; to bring forward in argument or as proof.

words.ex: He is an assiduous student who studies every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个勤奋的学生，每天都学习。
words.en: Someone who is assiduous works hard or does things very thoroughly.

words.ex: He felt antipathy toward the loud neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对那个吵闹的邻居感到反感。
words.en: A deep-seated feeling of dislike; aversion.

words.ex: He tries to assimilate new words every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天努力吸收新单词。
words.en: To assimilate means to take in and understand fully ideas, information, or culture, or to make something become part of a group or system.

words.ex: He tries to belittle his brother's success.
words.ex_cn: 他试图贬低他哥哥的成功。
words.en: To belittle someone or something means to make them seem less important or less good than they really are.

words.tr: v. 征募；征用；强占；霸占
words.ex: The soldiers commandeer the truck for their mission.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们征用了那辆卡车用于任务。
words.en: If the army, police, or any other group in authority commandeers a vehicle or building, they officially take charge of it so that they can use it.

words.tr: adj. 安静的；平静的；宁静的；
words.ex: The lake was tranquil in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 早晨的湖面很安静。
words.en: If a place or situation is tranquil, it is calm, peaceful, and quiet, with no disturbance or agitation.

words.ex: He endow a library with books.
words.ex_cn: 他捐赠了一图书馆的书。
words.en: If someone is endowed with a particular quality or ability, they naturally have it.

words.ex: He smiled at the recollection of his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他回忆起童年时微笑了。
words.en: The act of remembering something or the ability to remember.

words.ex: The balloon will ascend into the sky.
words.ex_cn: 气球将升上天空。
words.en: If you ascend a hill or staircase, you go up it. If a staircase or path ascends, it leads up to a higher place.

words.ex: He will enumerate the steps clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他将清晰地列出这些步骤。
words.en: To enumerate means to mention things one by one.

words.tr: v. 使麻痹；使瘫痪；使无效；使停止活动
words.ex: The accident paralyzed his leg.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故使他的腿瘫痪了。
words.en: If someone is paralyzed by an accident or an illness, they have no feeling in their body, or in part of their body, and are unable to move.

words.ex: The fairy tale features a dwarf who lives in a small house.
words.ex_cn: 这个童话故事中有一个住在小房子里的侏儒。
words.en: A dwarf is a person, animal, or plant that is much smaller than the usual size of its species. As a verb, to dwarf means to make someone or something seem small or insignificant in comparison.

words.ex: He disposed of the old books.
words.ex_cn: 他处理了那些旧书。
words.en: To dispose of something means to get rid of it, especially by throwing it away.

words.ex: The government wants to eradicate poverty.
words.ex_cn: 政府希望消灭贫困。
words.en: To eradicate something means to get rid of it completely.

words.ex: He is an apprentice in a car repair shop.
words.ex_cn: 他是汽车修理店的一名学徒。
words.en: An apprentice is a young person who works for someone in order to learn their skill.

words.tr: v. 增添活力；振奋；使活跃
words.ex: The fresh air invigorates me every morning.
words.ex_cn: 每天早晨的新鲜空气让我精神焕发。
words.en: If something invigorates you, it makes you feel more energetic and alive.

words.ex: The treacherous road made driving very scary.
words.ex_cn: 这条危险的道路让驾驶非常可怕。
words.en: If you describe someone as treacherous, you mean that they are likely to betray you and cannot be trusted. If you say that something is treacherous, you mean that it is very dangerous and unpredictable.

words.ex: His family's affluence allowed him to travel the world.
words.ex_cn: 他家的富裕让他能环游世界。
words.en: Affluence is the state of having a lot of money or owning many things.

words.ex: The two houses are adjacent to each other.
words.ex_cn: 这两栋房子彼此相邻。
words.en: If one thing is adjacent to another, it is next to it or adjoining it.

words.tr: adj. 全知的；无所不知的
words.ex: The omniscient narrator knows everything about the characters.
words.ex_cn: 全知的叙述者了解角色的一切。
words.en: Knowing everything; having infinite awareness, understanding, and insight.

words.ex: The hot weather enervates him.
words.ex_cn: 炎热的天气让他感到乏力。
words.en: If something enervates you, it makes you feel weak and lacking in energy.

words.ex: He bought a gift for his spouse.
words.ex_cn: 他给他的配偶买了一份礼物。
words.en: A spouse is a person's partner in marriage.

words.ex: He wants to expedite the process.
words.ex_cn: 他想加快这个过程。
words.en: To expedite something means to make it happen or be done more quickly.

words.tr: n. 音乐会；演奏会；一致；和谐；
words.ex: We went to a concert last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚去听了音乐会。
words.en: A concert is a performance of music by one or more musicians or singers, which usually takes place in the evening.

words.ex: He inherited a house from his father.
words.ex_cn: 他从父亲那里继承了一所房子。
words.en: If you inherit something such as a trait, characteristic, or quality, you are born with it, because your parents or ancestors had it. If you inherit money or property, you receive it from someone who has died.

words.tr: adj. 精明练达的；有远见的；有洞察力的
words.ex: He is a sagacious man who always makes wise choices.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个睿智的人，总是做出明智的选择。
words.en: Having or showing keen mental discernment and good judgment; shrewd.

words.ex: He exerted pressure on his team to win.
words.ex_cn: 他给他的团队施加了压力以赢得比赛。
words.en: To exert means to use power, influence, or effort to make something happen.

words.ex: Finding my lost keys while walking in the park was pure serendipity.
words.ex_cn: 在公园散步时偶然找到了丢失的钥匙，这真是易遇奇缘的运气。
words.en: The occurrence and development of events by chance in a happy or beneficial way.

words.tr: adj. 资源丰富的；机敏的；足智多谋的
words.ex: He is a resourceful man who can fix anything with little material.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个资源丰富的男人，能用很少的材料修好任何东西。
words.en: If someone is resourceful, they are good at finding ways of dealing with problems.

words.tr: v. 发芽；长出；迅速成长；涌现；
words.ex: The seed will sprout in spring.
words.ex_cn: 这颗种子会在春天发芽。
words.en: If a plant sprouts, or if it sprouts something, it produces new leaves or buds.

words.tr:
v. 中断；暂停；
n. 停顿下来；
words.ex: The storm halted the flight.
words.ex_cn: 风暴中断了航班。
words.en: to bring or come to a stop; a temporary or permanent stop

words.ex: Don't jeopardize your health by skipping meals.
words.ex_cn: 不要因为不吃饭而危及你的健康。
words.en: To jeopardize something means to do something that may destroy it or cause it to be lost.

words.ex: He is conversant with basic math.
words.ex_cn: 他熟悉基础数学。
words.en: If you are conversant with something, you are familiar with it and able to deal with it.

words.tr: n. 权宜；与目的相称；私利
words.ex: He ignored the rules for expediency.
words.ex_cn: 他为了方便而忽略了规则。
words.en: Expediency is the quality of being convenient and practical despite possibly being improper or immoral.

words.tr:
n. 最高统治者；君主；元首
adj. 独立自主的；拥有最高统治权的
words.ex: The sovereign makes important decisions for the country.
words.ex_cn: 君主为国家做出重要决定。
words.en: A sovereign is a king, queen, or other supreme ruler.

words.ex: He always follows the maxim 'work hard, play hard'.
words.ex_cn: 他总是遵循‘努力工作，尽情玩耍’这一信条。
words.en: A maxim is a short, easily remembered expression of a basic principle, general truth, or rule of conduct.

words.ex: He dwells in a small house near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他住在湖边的一所小房子里。
words.en: If you dwell on something, especially something unpleasant, you think, speak, or write about it a lot or for quite a long time.

words.ex: The dark clouds are a harbinger of storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云是暴风雨的预兆。
words.en: A harbinger is something that shows that something is going to happen soon, especially something bad.

words.tr: adj. 煽动性的；煽动叛变的
words.ex: The speech was deemed seditious and led to his arrest.
words.ex_cn: 这次演讲被认为是煽动性的，导致他被捕。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as seditious, you mean that they are likely to cause people to rebel against the authority of the state.

words.ex: He tried to detach himself from the group.
words.ex_cn: 他试图脱离这个群体。
words.en: If you detach one thing from another that it is fixed to, you remove it. If one thing detaches from another, it becomes separated from it.

words.tr: adj. 散漫的；不着边际的
words.ex: He gave a discursive speech about many topics.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一篇关于许多主题的散漫演讲。
words.en: If a style of writing or speech is discursive, it includes a lot of information that is not relevant to the main subject.

words.ex: His oversight caused the project to fail.
words.ex_cn: 他的疏忽导致项目失败。
words.en: An oversight is a mistake that is made by not noticing something or by forgetting to do something.

words.ex: The teacher intervened when the students argued.
words.ex_cn: 当学生们争吵时，老师进行了干涉。
words.en: If you intervene in a situation, you become involved in it and try to change it.

words.ex: He lost his job because of his integrity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为正直而失去了工作。
words.en: Integrity is the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles.

words.tr: adj. 休眠的；蛰伏的；暂停活动的
words.ex: The volcano is dormant now.
words.ex_cn: 这座火山现在处于休眠状态。
words.en: Something that is dormant is not active or growing but has the ability to be active at a later time.

words.ex: Saint Francis loved animals and helped the poor.
words.ex_cn: 圣方济各热爱动物并帮助穷人。
words.en: A saint is a person who is recognized as having an exceptional degree of holiness, likeness, or closeness to God.

words.tr: adj. 痛切的；酸楚的；强烈的；尖刻的
words.ex: The letter was poignant and made her cry.
words.ex_cn: 这封信很感人，让她哭了。
words.en: A poignant piece of writing or music makes you feel sad or full of pity.

words.tr: v. （以可望而不可及之物）逗引；使干着急
words.ex: The smell of cookies tantalize him.
words.ex_cn: 饼干的香味让他垂涎欲滴。
words.en: If someone or something tantalizes you, they make you feel hopeful and excited about getting what you want, usually before disappointing you by not letting you have it.

words.tr: adj. 相接的；相邻的；接壤的
words.ex: The two countries are contiguous.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家是相邻的。
words.en: Being in contact; touching or next to each other.

words.ex: The law will emancipate slaves.
words.ex_cn: 法律将解放奴隶。
words.en: To emancipate someone means to set them free from something that restricts their freedom to do what they want.

words.tr:
n. 猛跌；衰退；萧条期
v. 急剧下降；暴跌；重重地坐下（或倒下）
words.ex: The company's sales went into a slump last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月，这家公司的销售额下滑了。
words.en: If something such as the value of something slumps, it falls suddenly and by a large amount.

words.tr: n. 异于一般情况的人（或事物）
words.ex: The number 100 is an outlier in this data set.
words.ex_cn: 在这个数据集中，数字100是一个异常值。
words.en: An outlier is a person or thing that is atypical within a particular group, class, or category.

words.ex: His lectures were marked by erudition and wit.
words.ex_cn: 他的讲座以博学和机智著称。
words.en: Erudition is the quality of having or showing great knowledge or learning.

words.ex: He felt the stigma of being unemployed.
words.ex_cn: 他感受到了失业的耻辱。
words.en: A stigma is a strong feeling of disapproval that most people in a society have about something, especially when this is unfair.

words.ex: He fabricates excuses to avoid work.
words.ex_cn: 他编造借口来逃避工作。
words.en: To fabricate means to invent or produce something false in order to deceive someone.

words.tr: v. 发音；宣告；“pronounce”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 显著的；
words.ex: He pronounced the word correctly.
words.ex_cn: 他正确地发音了这个单词。
words.en: Something that is pronounced is very noticeable or obvious.

words.tr:
v. 使翘棱；使扭曲变形
n. 弯曲；歪曲
words.ex: The heat will warp the metal.
words.ex_cn: 热量会使金属变形。
words.en: To warp is to bend or twist something out of its natural shape, often as a result of heat or moisture. It can also refer to the state of being bent or twisted.

words.ex: They conspire to cheat on the test.
words.ex_cn: 他们密谋在考试中作弊。
words.en: If two or more people or groups conspire to do something illegal or harmful, they make a secret agreement to do it.

words.ex: He squandered all his money on games.
words.ex_cn: 他把所有的钱都浪费在游戏上了。
words.en: If you squander money, resources, or opportunities, you waste them in a foolish or careless way.

words.tr: v. 暗指；（间接）提到；影射
words.ex: He alluded to the problem without naming it.
words.ex_cn: 他暗示了这个问题，但没有点明。
words.en: To allude to something means to mention it in an indirect way.

words.tr: adj. 有狂风暴雨的；狂暴的
words.ex: The tempestuous sea made the voyage dangerous.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨的海面使得航行变得危险。
words.en: If you describe a relationship or a situation as tempestuous, you mean that it is full of strong emotions, especially anger or passion.

words.tr: n. 几率；不利条件；不平等；
words.ex: The odds of winning the lottery are very low.
words.ex_cn: 中彩票的几率非常低。
words.en: The odds are the chances that a particular thing will happen.

words.tr: n. 必然的结果（或结论）；推论
words.ex: The theorem leads to a simple corollary.
words.ex_cn: 这个定理引出了一个简单的推论。
words.en: A corollary is a statement that follows on from another statement, and that is usually easily understood or proved.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生的；迫在眉睫的； v. “impend”的现在分词；
words.ex: An impending storm made people stay indoors.
words.ex_cn: 一场即将发生的风暴让人们待在室内。
words.en: If an event or situation is impending, it is about to happen or is likely to happen very soon.

words.tr:
v. 利用；
n. 水龙头；轻拍；轻敲；轻击；
words.ex: The company tapped local talent to grow its business.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司利用本地人才来发展业务。
words.en: If you tap something, you hit it with a quick light blow or a series of quick light blows. A tap is a device that controls the flow of a liquid or gas from a pipe or container, for example on a sink.

words.tr: adj. 偏离规则的；反常的
words.ex: The temperature was anomalous for this season.
words.ex_cn: 这个季节的温度异常。
words.en: Deviating from what is standard, normal, or expected.

words.tr:
n. 大洪水；暴雨；泛滥
v. 泛滥；大量涌入
words.ex: The rain caused a deluge in the town.
words.ex_cn: 这场雨在镇上引发了洪水。
words.en: A deluge is a severe flood or a very heavy fall of rain that causes a lot of damage.

words.ex: She loves to follow the latest fashion.
words.ex_cn: 她喜欢追随最新的时尚。
words.en: Fashion is a popular style of clothes, hair, etc. at a particular time.

words.ex: He is clumsy and dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他很笨拙，把玻璃杯打翻了。
words.en: A clumsy person moves or handles things in a careless, awkward way, often so that things are knocked over or broken.

words.ex: He proved his innocence to vindicate his name.
words.ex_cn: 他证明了自己的清白以洗清自己的名声。
words.en: To clear someone of blame or suspicion.

words.ex: The city's sprawl has covered many farmlands.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的杂乱无序的拓展覆盖了许多农田。
words.en: If you sprawl somewhere, you sit or lie with your legs and arms spread out in a careless way.

words.tr: v. 系上；附加；使相关；使依附；隶属于；“attach”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 附属的；附加的；依恋的；
words.ex: He attached the leash to the dog's collar.
words.ex_cn: 他把狗绳系在狗的项圈上。
words.en: If you say that one thing is attached to another, you mean that the two things are connected, either physically or because they are related in some way.

words.tr:
v. 发扑哧声；嘎吱嘎吱的走；压制；遏制
n. 嘎吱声；扑哧声
words.ex: He tried to squelch the rumors about him.
words.ex_cn: 他试图压制关于他的谣言。
words.en: To squelch means to suppress or silence something, often forcefully, or to make a sucking sound as when walking through mud.

words.ex: The teacher reprehended the student for his disruptive behavior.
words.ex_cn: 老师因学生扰乱课堂的行为而责备他。
words.en: If you reprehend someone, you criticize them severely for their actions or behavior.

words.tr:
n. 发酵；酵素；动乱
v. （使）发酵；动乱
words.ex: The ferment of yeast makes bread rise.
words.ex_cn: 酵母的发酵使面包膨胀。
words.en: If a substance ferments or if it is fermented, it changes chemically because of the action of yeast or bacteria, often producing alcohol.

words.tr:
adj. 被剥夺的；丧失的；失去亲人的
v. 夺去；使丧失；“bereave”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He was bereft of words after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他一句话也说不出来。
words.en: If someone is bereft of something, they have lost it and feel its loss keenly.

words.ex: He had a minor ailment and stayed home from work.
words.ex_cn: 他得了一点小病，没去上班。
words.en: An ailment is a minor illness or health problem.

words.ex: He spoke in a polite manner.
words.ex_cn: 他以礼貌的方式说话。
words.en: The way in which something is done or happens.

words.tr:
n. 刻板印象；陈规老套
v. 对…存有成见；把…模式化
words.ex: He broke the stereotype that boys cannot cry.
words.ex_cn: 他打破了男孩不能哭的刻板印象。
words.en: A stereotype is a fixed general image or set of characteristics that a lot of people believe represent a particular type of person or thing.

words.tr: adj. 完全的；荒凉的；光秃秃的；僵硬的；严厉的
words.ex: There was a stark difference between the two results.
words.ex_cn: 这两个结果之间有完全的差异。
words.en: Stark means complete, severe, or obvious in a way that is impossible to avoid noticing.

words.ex: They deem this plan too risky.
words.ex_cn: 他们认为这个计划太冒险了。
words.en: If you deem something to be the case, you consider that it is the case.

words.ex: The gang tried to extort money from the shop owner.
words.ex_cn: 这个帮派试图向店主敲诈钱财。
words.en: To extort is to obtain something, especially money, through force, threats, or other unfair means.

words.tr:
n. 有志者；立志…的人
adj. 有野心的；有抱负的
words.ex: He is an aspirant for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他是这份工作的求职者。
words.en: An aspirant is someone who is ambitious and eager to achieve a particular goal or position.

words.ex: This brand has an exclusive design.
words.ex_cn: 这个品牌拥有独有的设计。
words.en: Something that is exclusive is available only to particular people, and not to everyone.

words.ex: They have a reciprocal agreement to help each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们有一个互相帮助的互惠协议。
words.en: A reciprocal action or agreement involves two people or groups who do the same thing to each other or agree to help each other in a similar way.

words.tr: n. 派系；派系斗争；内讧
words.ex: The faction argued loudly about the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 这个派别就新规定激烈争论。
words.en: A faction is a group of people within a larger group who have different opinions and beliefs from the rest of the group.

words.ex: Please stir the soup before serving.
words.ex_cn: 请在上菜前搅拌一下汤。
words.en: To mix a substance or move it around using a spoon or other object; to cause to move or act; to arouse or excite.

words.tr:
v. 细述；叙述
n. 叙述；重新计票
words.ex: He tried to recount the accident to the police.
words.ex_cn: 他试图向警察重新叙述那场事故。
words.en: To recount means to tell someone about something that happened, often in detail; or to count something again to make sure the number is correct.

words.ex: He wrote the book for posterity.
words.ex_cn: 他写这本书是为了留给后人。
words.en: All future generations of people.

words.ex: He found himself in a predicament when he lost his wallet.
words.ex_cn: 当他丢掉钱包时，他陷入了困境。
words.en: A predicament is a difficult, perplexing, or trying situation.

words.ex: He is the protagonist in the story.
words.ex_cn: 他是故事中的主角。
words.en: The main character in a story, play, film, etc., especially the one who is good or who the audience is expected to support.

words.ex: Children develop cognitive skills as they grow.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在成长过程中发展认知能力。
words.en: Cognitive means relating to the mental process involved in knowing, learning, and understanding things.

words.ex: Their argument was acrimonious and lasted all night.
words.ex_cn: 他们的争论很尖刻，持续了一整晚。
words.en: If you say that an argument or conversation is acrimonious, you mean that it is bitter and angry because the people involved disagree with each other.

words.tr:
n. 情节；小块用地；
v. 绘图；
words.ex: The plot of the movie was very exciting.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的情节非常精彩。
words.en: A plot is a secret plan by a group of people to do something that is illegal or wrong, especially against a person or a government. It can also refer to the main events of a play, novel, movie, or similar work, devised and presented by the writer as an interrelated sequence. Additionally, a plot can be a small piece of land that is used or intended for a specific purpose.

words.tr: adj. 文雅的；有教养的；上流社会的；装绅士派头的
words.ex: She spoke in a genteel way at the dinner party.
words.ex_cn: 她在晚宴上说话很文雅。
words.en: Someone who is genteel behaves in a polite and refined way, often in a manner that is considered typical of someone from a high social class.

words.ex: The city is at a latitude of 40 degrees north.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市位于北纬40度。
words.en: Latitude is the distance of a place north or south of the equator, measured in degrees.

words.ex: The boss can override the rules if needed.
words.ex_cn: 如果需要，老板可以凌驾于规则之上。
words.en: If one thing in a situation overrides other things, it is more important than them.

words.ex: The teacher elucidated the math problem with a simple diagram.
words.ex_cn: 老师用一个简单的图表阐明了这道数学题。
words.en: To make something clear or easy to understand by explaining or giving reasons.

words.tr:
n. 账户；叙述；账目；
v. 占…；说明；
words.ex: I opened a bank account last week.
words.ex_cn: 我上周开了一家银行账户。
words.en: An account is a detailed report or description of an event or situation.

words.tr: v. 兑现；递送；交付；发表；为…接生；
words.ex: He promised to deliver on his goal.
words.ex_cn: 他承诺要兑现自己的目标。
words.en: To bring and hand over (a letter, parcel, or ordered goods) to the proper recipient or address.

words.tr:
n. 成分；
adj. 构成的；
words.ex: Sugar is a constituent of soda.
words.ex_cn: 糖是苏打水的一种成分。
words.en: A constituent is a part of a whole. In politics, a constituent is a person who is represented by an elected official.

words.ex: He feared retribution for his actions.
words.ex_cn: 他害怕因自己的行为而受到报复。
words.en: Retribution is punishment for a crime, especially punishment that is carried out by someone other than the official authorities.

words.ex: The two kids stayed in equilibrium on the seesaw.
words.ex_cn: 两个孩子在跷跷板上保持了平衡。
words.en: A state in which opposing forces or influences are balanced.

words.ex: They had an amicable talk after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 争吵之后，他们进行了一次友好的交谈。
words.en: When people have an amicable relationship, they are pleasant towards each other and solve their problems without arguing.

words.ex: He is averse to changing his routine.
words.ex_cn: 他反对改变自己的日常安排。
words.en: If you say that someone is averse to something, you mean they dislike it or have a strong opposition to it.

words.tr: v. 证明…是真实的；鉴别
words.ex: He must authenticate his identity with a password.
words.ex_cn: 他必须用密码验证自己的身份。
words.en: To authenticate something means to prove or confirm that it is genuine or true.

words.tr: v. 起绰号；把…称作；配音；译制
words.ex: They dubbed him 'Captain Cool' for his calm style.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他冷静的风格给他起了个绰号叫‘冷静队长’。
words.en: To give a name, title, or nickname to someone or something; to provide a film or television program with a soundtrack in a different language from the original.

words.tr:
n. 度假胜地；手段；
v. 求助于；
words.ex: They went to a beach resort for their vacation.
words.ex_cn: 他们去一个海滨度假胜地度假。
words.en: If you resort to a particular course of action, you do it because you cannot see any other way of achieving what you want.

words.ex: The resilient child bounced back quickly after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 这个适应力强的孩子在事故后很快恢复了。
words.en: Something that is resilient is strong and not easily damaged by being hit, stretched, or squeezed.

words.tr: adj. 自命不凡的；自负的；矫饰的
words.ex: He wore a fancy hat to seem pretentious.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶华丽的帽子，显得自命不凡。
words.en: If you describe something as pretentious, you mean that it is intended to seem important or significant, but you think it is not.

words.tr:
v. 想要；
adj. 花哨的；昂贵的；
n. 爱好；
words.ex: I fancy a cup of tea.
words.ex_cn: 我想要一杯茶。
words.en: If you describe something as fancy, you mean that it is special, unusual, or elaborate, often because it has a lot of decoration or is very expensive.

words.tr: adj. 疑惑的；嘲弄的；揶揄的
words.ex: He gave a quizzical look when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他露出困惑的表情。
words.en: If you give someone a quizzical look or smile, you look at them or smile at them in a way that shows that you are surprised or amused by their behavior.

words.tr:
n. 天主教徒；
adj. 天主教的；
words.ex: He is a catholic who goes to church every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名每周日都去教堂的天主教徒。
words.en: If you describe a collection of things or people as catholic, you are emphasizing that it is varied and includes many different types of things or people.

words.ex: I concur with your opinion.
words.ex_cn: 我同意你的观点。
words.en: If one person concurs with another person, the first person agrees with the second person.

words.ex: He has a chronic cough that lasts for months.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个持续数月的慢性咳嗽。
words.en: A chronic illness or condition lasts for a long time and cannot be cured, but it can usually be controlled.

words.ex: He accepted liability for the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他承担了事故的责任。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is a liability, you mean that they cause a lot of problems or embarrassment.

words.ex: The computer will execute the program quickly.
words.ex_cn: 计算机将快速执行该程序。
words.en: To execute means to carry out or put into effect a plan, order, or course of action. It can also refer to the act of legally killing someone as a punishment.

words.tr: adj. 平静的；宁静的；温和的；
words.ex: The lake was placid in the morning light.
words.ex_cn: 清晨的阳光下，湖面平静无波。
words.en: A placid person or animal is calm and does not easily become excited, angry, or upset.

words.ex: The smoke came out of the vent.
words.ex_cn: 烟从排气口飘了出来。
words.en: A vent is a hole or opening that allows air, gas, or liquid to pass out of or into a confined space.

words.tr:
n. 杂交种；混合物；
adj. 混合的；
words.ex: The corn hybrid grows faster than the old type.
words.ex_cn: 这种玉米杂交种比旧品种长得更快。
words.en: A hybrid is a plant or animal that has been produced from two different types of plant or animal, especially to get better characteristics. It can also refer to something that is a mixture of two different things.

words.tr: adj. 令人惊愕的； v. “stagger”的现在分词；
words.ex: The staggering cost of the project surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目令人惊愕的费用让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: Something that is staggering is very surprising and shocking.

words.tr: adj. 沙哑的；粗声的；喧闹的
words.ex: His raucous voice made it hard to understand him.
words.ex_cn: 他沙哑的声音让他很难被听清楚。
words.en: A raucous sound is loud and harsh.

words.ex: The hen incubate eggs until they hatch.
words.ex_cn: 母鸡孵化鸡蛋直到小鸡孵出。
words.en: to keep eggs warm so that they develop and hatch, or to keep cells, bacteria, etc. at a suitable temperature so that they develop

words.ex: His idiosyncrasy is talking to himself while reading.
words.ex_cn: 他的怪癖是读书时自言自语。
words.en: An idiosyncrasy is a peculiar or unusual habit, way of behaving, or feature that someone or something has.

words.tr: n. 岩屑；碎石；沙砾；风化物；残余物
words.ex: The garden is full of dry leaves and detritus.
words.ex_cn: 花园里到处都是枯叶和碎屑。
words.en: Detritus refers to the debris or waste material that results from the disintegration or wearing away of something, such as rock or organic matter.

words.ex: His repertoire includes singing, dancing, and acting.
words.ex_cn: 他的全部才能包括唱歌、跳舞和表演。
words.en: A repertoire is all the plays, songs, pieces of music, etc. that a performer or group knows and can perform.

words.ex: He swore allegiance to his country.
words.ex_cn: 他向自己的国家宣誓效忠。
words.en: Loyalty or commitment to a superior or to a group or cause.

words.tr: adj. 最高的；至上的；最重要的；
words.ex: His safety is paramount.
words.ex_cn: 他的安全是最重要的。
words.en: Something that is paramount or of paramount importance is more important than anything else.

words.tr: n. 贵族政治；贵族统治；贵族
words.ex: The aristocracy lived in big castles long ago.
words.ex_cn: 很久以前，贵族住在巨大的城堡里。
words.en: The highest class in certain societies, especially those holding hereditary titles or offices.

words.tr: adj. 有希望的；有前途的； v. 承诺；答应；“promise”的现在分词；
words.ex: The young boy is a promising student.
words.ex_cn: 这个小男孩是个有希望的学生。
words.en: Showing signs of future success or achievement.

words.ex: The teacher will allocate books to students.
words.ex_cn: 老师将给学生分配书籍。
words.en: To allocate something means to give it to a particular person or use it for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The store made an inventory of all the products.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有商品做了一份清单。
words.en: An inventory is a detailed list of all the items in a place.

words.ex: He crossed the threshold of adulthood at 18.
words.ex_cn: 他在18岁时进入了成年的起始点。
words.en: The threshold of something is the point at which it begins or changes.

words.tr: n. 自我主义；利己主义
words.ex: His egotism makes him talk only about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他的自我中心让他只谈论自己。
words.en: Egotism is the practice of talking and thinking about oneself excessively because of an undue sense of self-importance.

words.tr: v. 公开放弃；发誓断绝
words.ex: He had to abjure his old beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不放弃他的旧信仰。
words.en: If you abjure something such as a belief or way of life, you state publicly that you will give it up or that you reject it.

words.tr: n. 脆弱性；脆性；易碎性
words.ex: The fragility of the glass made it easy to break.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃的易碎性让它很容易破碎。
words.en: The quality of being easily broken or damaged.

words.ex: He inherited his ancestral land from his grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他从祖父那里继承了祖传的土地。
words.en: Something that is ancestral relates to ancestors or to something that has been passed down from ancestors.

words.ex: The boy hurt his spine when he fell from the tree.
words.ex_cn: 他从树上摔下来时伤到了脊柱。
words.en: The spine is the row of bones down the center of your back that supports your body and protects your spinal cord.

words.ex: His incisive comment solved the problem quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他一针见血的评论迅速解决了问题。
words.en: An incisive remark, question, or piece of writing is very clear and direct, and shows that the person understands something very well.

words.ex: He looked at the lie with contempt.
words.ex_cn: 他轻蔑地看着这个谎言。
words.en: If you have contempt for someone or something, you have no respect for them or think that they are unimportant.

words.tr: adj. 深沉响亮的；洪亮的
words.ex: The bell rang with a sonorous sound.
words.ex_cn: 钟发出洪亮的声音。
words.en: A sonorous sound is deep, full, and rich, often pleasing to the ear.

words.tr: n. 一致同意；全体赞同
words.ex: The team showed unanimity in voting for the new plan.
words.ex_cn: 团队在投票支持新计划时意见一致。
words.en: Unanimity is complete agreement among all members of a group.

words.tr: v. 哄；用好话劝诱；哄骗
words.ex: He tried to coax the cat out from under the bed.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄猫从床底下出来。
words.en: To coax someone means to persuade them to do something by gentle persuasion or flattery.

words.tr: adj. 倾向一方的；不平衡的；悬殊的
words.ex: The game was lopsided, and one team won by 10 points.
words.ex_cn: 这场比赛比分悬殊，一支队伍以10分获胜。
words.en: Something that is lopsided is uneven because one side is lower or heavier than the other.

words.tr: adj. 红润的；华丽的；过分装饰的
words.ex: Her cheeks were florid after running in the cold.
words.ex_cn: 她在寒冷中跑步后，脸颊变得红润。
words.en: If you describe something as florid, you mean that it is complicated and elaborate rather than plain and simple.

words.tr: adj. 可感知的；易察觉的；明显的
words.ex: The tension in the room was palpable.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的紧张感是明显的。
words.en: If you describe something as palpable, you mean that it is obvious or intense and easily noticed.

words.tr: n. 高超的技艺；造诣；英勇；
words.ex: His prowess in basketball amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在篮球方面的高超技艺让所有人都惊叹。
words.en: Exceptional skill or ability in a particular field or activity.

words.ex: The soup was palatable after adding salt.
words.ex_cn: 加了盐后，汤变得可口美味了。
words.en: If you describe food or drink as palatable, you mean that it tastes pleasant.

words.tr: v. 同意；继承；即位；加入
words.ex: He acceded to their request.
words.ex_cn: 他同意了他们的请求。
words.en: If you accede to someone's request, you do what they ask.

words.tr: n. 迷信；迷信观念（或思想）；
words.ex: He avoids walking under ladders because of superstition.
words.ex_cn: 他因为迷信而不愿从梯子下走过。
words.en: A superstition is a belief or practice resulting from ignorance, fear of the unknown, trust in magic or chance, or a false conception of causation.

words.ex: The doctor prescribed medicine for my cold.
words.ex_cn: 医生给我开了治疗感冒的药。
words.en: If a doctor prescribes medicine or treatment for you, he or she tells you what medicine or treatment to have.

words.ex: The ancient symbol remains an enigma.
words.ex_cn: 这个古代符号仍然是一个谜。
words.en: An enigma is something that is mysterious and difficult to understand.

words.ex: Hiking up the mountain was a strenuous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰苦的任务。
words.en: Requiring or using great effort or exertion.

words.tr:
v. 加酵母；使发酵；影响
n. 酵素；酵母；潜移默化的影响
words.ex: She uses yeast to leaven the bread.
words.ex_cn: 她用酵母使面包发酵。
words.en: Leaven is a substance, typically yeast, that is used in dough to make it rise. It can also refer to something that modifies or lightens a situation or atmosphere.

words.tr: v. 反复地说；重申；重述
words.ex: He reiterate that he is sorry.
words.ex_cn: 他反复地说他很抱歉。
words.en: If you reiterate something, you say it again, usually in order to emphasize it.

words.ex: This small enterprise makes handmade toys.
words.ex_cn: 这家小企业生产手工玩具。
words.en: An enterprise is a company or business, often a large one, or a difficult or important project, especially one that involves a lot of planning and organization.

words.ex: The stomach digests food into nutrients.
words.ex_cn: 胃将食物消化成营养物质。
words.en: To digest means to break down food in the stomach and intestines into substances that can be absorbed by the body. It can also mean to understand or assimilate information. As a noun, it refers to a compilation or summary of information.

words.tr:
adj. 有害的；恶意的
v. 中伤；污蔑
words.ex: The virus is malign and spreads quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒是有害的，并且传播迅速。
words.en: If you malign someone, you say unpleasant and untrue things about them. If something is malign, it is harmful or evil.

words.ex: The queen's reign lasted 70 years.
words.ex_cn: 女王的统治持续了70年。
words.en: The period during which a sovereign rules; to hold royal office; to prevail

words.tr: v. 沉思；闷闷不乐地想；n. 一窝幼崽；沉思的状态
words.ex: He sits by the window and broods over his failures.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在窗边，为自己的失败而忧思。
words.en: If someone broods over something, they think about it a lot, seriously and often unhappily. A brood is a group of young birds all born at the same time to the same mother.

words.ex: The earthquake devastated the small town.
words.ex_cn: 地震摧毁了这个小镇。
words.en: To devastate means to destroy or ruin something completely, or to cause someone to feel extreme sadness or shock.

words.tr: n. 陈词滥调；老生常谈；
words.ex: His speech was full of platitudes about hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了关于努力工作的陈词滥调。
words.en: A platitude is a statement that has been used so often that it is meaningless and shows a lack of original thought.

words.ex: The indigenous people live in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 本土居民住在森林里。
words.en: Indigenous people or things belong to the country in which they are found, rather than coming there or being brought there from another country.

words.tr: adj. 全世界的；四海一家的；
words.ex: This city has a cosmopolitan population.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市有着来自世界各地的人口。
words.en: A cosmopolitan place or society is full of people from many different countries and cultures.

words.tr:
n. 纪律；学科；科目；训练；惩戒；
v. 约束自己；
words.ex: The teacher enforced discipline in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 老师在教室里维持纪律。
words.en: Discipline is the practice of making people obey rules or standards of behaviour, and punishing them when they do not.

words.ex: He shows piety by praying every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天祈祷，表现出虔诚。
words.en: Piety is strong religious belief, or behaviour that is religious or morally correct.

words.tr: adj. 没注意到的；未觉察的；忘却的；
words.ex: He was oblivious to the noise around him.
words.ex_cn: 他对周围的噪音毫无察觉。
words.en: If you are oblivious to something or oblivious of it, you are not aware of it.

words.tr: n. 分支；支流；衍生物；后果
words.ex: The ramification of the tree spread wide.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树的分支延伸得很广。
words.en: A ramification is a complex or unwelcome consequence of an action or decision.

words.ex: The tailor made a new suit for the man.
words.ex_cn: 裁缝为这位男士做了一套新西装。
words.en: A tailor is a person whose job is to make men's clothes, especially suits, jackets, and trousers, that fit individual customers. As a verb, to tailor means to make or adapt something for a particular purpose or person.

words.ex: The upshot of the meeting was a new plan.
words.ex_cn: 会议的结果是一个新计划。
words.en: The final result or outcome of a situation or event.

words.ex: With hindsight, I should have saved more money.
words.ex_cn: 事后看来，我本该多存些钱。
words.en: The understanding of a situation or event only after it has happened or developed.

words.tr: n. 前任；前辈；原有事物
words.ex: He became the new manager, replacing his predecessor.
words.ex_cn: 他成为了新经理，接替了他的前任。
words.en: A predecessor is someone who had a job or a position before someone else, or something that comes before another thing in time or in a series.

words.tr:
adj. 极重要的；
n. 紧急的事；
words.ex: It is imperative to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水非常重要。
words.en: If it is imperative that something is done, that thing is extremely important and must be done.

words.tr: adj. 可憎的；讨厌的；令人作呕的
words.ex: The smell of the garbage was odious.
words.ex_cn: 垃圾的气味令人讨厌。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as odious, you think that they are extremely unpleasant, horrible, or disgusting.

words.tr: adj. 即兴的；临时的；非预谋的
words.ex: He gave an extemporary speech without notes.
words.ex_cn: 他没有稿子即兴发表了演讲。

words.tr:
v. 移居国外；把…逐出国外
n. 侨民；移居国外者
adj. 移居国外的；被逐出国外的
words.ex: He decided to expatriate to Canada for a better life.
words.ex_cn: 他决定移居加拿大以追求更好的生活。
words.en: An expatriate is someone who lives in a country that is not their own, often for work or political reasons.

words.ex: He execrates lies and dishonesty.
words.ex_cn: 他痛恨谎言和不诚实。
words.en: To express great loathing for; to curse or denounce vehemently.

words.tr: v. 背叛；出卖；泄露；暴露
words.ex: He betrays his friend by telling the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他通过泄露秘密背叛了朋友。
words.en: If you betray someone who loves or trusts you, your actions hurt and disappoint them.

words.tr:
n. 藏物处；隐藏物；
v. 匿藏；
words.ex: The hunters found a cache of food under the rocks.
words.ex_cn: 猎人们在石头下发现了一个食物藏匿处。
words.en: A cache is a hidden store of things such as weapons or a supply of food.

words.ex: The table was replete with food.
words.ex_cn: 桌子上摆满了食物。
words.en: If you are replete with something, you have a lot of it and it fills you up.

words.tr:
n. 被愚弄的人；容易受骗的人
v. 欺骗；诈骗；愚弄
words.ex: He was duped into buying a fake watch.
words.ex_cn: 他被骗去买了一块假手表。
words.en: A dupe is someone who is easily deceived or cheated, often because they are too trusting. As a verb, to dupe means to deceive or trick someone into believing something that is not true.

words.tr:
n. 冒险事业；商业冒险；投机；
v. 冒险；投机；
words.ex: He started a new venture in technology.
words.ex_cn: 他创办了一项新的科技冒险事业。
words.en: If you venture somewhere, you go somewhere that might be dangerous. If you venture a question or statement, you say it in an uncertain way because you are afraid it might be stupid or wrong.

words.ex: His ulterior motive was to get money.
words.ex_cn: 他别有用心，目的是弄到钱。
words.en: If you say that someone has an ulterior motive for doing something, you believe that they have a hidden reason for doing it.

words.ex: The sun descends behind the hills.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在山后落下。
words.en: If you descend or if you descend a staircase, you move downwards from a higher to a lower level.

words.ex: The clown made a comical face and everyone laughed.
words.ex_cn: 小丑做了一个可笑的表情，大家都笑了。
words.en: If you describe something as comical, you mean that it is amusing and makes you laugh.

words.ex: His legacy includes many charity schools.
words.ex_cn: 他的遗产包括许多慈善学校。
words.en: Something handed down from an ancestor or a predecessor or from the past.

words.tr: adj. 平民的；卑贱的；卑鄙的；不光彩的
words.ex: He came from an ignoble family, but worked hard to succeed.
words.ex_cn: 他出身于平民家庭，但努力工作以取得成功。
words.en: If you describe something as ignoble, you mean that it is bad and something to be ashamed of.

words.tr:
n. 带位员；接待员；门房
v. 引领；招待；做招待员
words.ex: The usher showed us to our seats in the theater.
words.ex_cn: 带位员带我们到了剧院的座位。
words.en: An usher is someone who shows people where to sit, especially at a formal event such as a wedding or a concert. As a verb, to usher means to show someone where to go or to lead them somewhere.

words.ex: His pride begets conflict.
words.ex_cn: 他的骄傲招致了冲突。
words.en: To beget means to cause something to happen or exist.

words.ex: He is upbeat about his new job.
words.ex_cn: 他对新工作感到乐观。
words.en: If people or their opinions are upbeat, they are cheerful and full of hope.

words.ex: He is a connoisseur of fine wine.
words.ex_cn: 他是优质葡萄酒的行家。
words.en: A connoisseur is a person who is especially competent to pass critical judgments in an art, particularly one of the fine arts, or in matters of taste.

words.ex: His smile evinces joy.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑流露出快乐。
words.en: To show clearly that you have a particular quality, feeling, or ability.

words.ex: The judge will adjudicate the dispute next week.
words.ex_cn: 法官将在下周裁决这场纠纷。
words.en: To adjudicate means to make an official decision about a problem or dispute.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；目空一切的；自大的
words.ex: He gave a supercilious smile when she asked a simple question.
words.ex_cn: 当她问了一个简单的问题时，他露出了傲慢的微笑。
words.en: If you say that someone is supercilious, you disapprove of them because they behave in a way that shows they think they are better than other people.

words.ex: The news will disseminate quickly through social media.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻会通过社交媒体迅速传播。
words.en: To disseminate means to spread or distribute something, especially information, widely.

words.ex: The municipality cleaned the streets last week.
words.ex_cn: 这个自治市上周清理了街道。
words.en: A municipality is a city or town that has its own government to manage local affairs.

words.ex: Water can penetrate the soil slowly.
words.ex_cn: 水可以慢慢渗透进土壤。
words.en: To penetrate means to enter or pass through something, especially when this is difficult or when it is not obvious how to do it.

words.ex: The scientist tried to replicate the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家试图复制这个实验。
words.en: To replicate something means to do or make something again in exactly the same way.

words.tr:
n. 编年史；年代记
v. 按时间顺序记录
words.ex: He writes a chronicle of his daily life.
words.ex_cn: 他记录自己每天的生活。
words.en: A chronicle is a historical account of events arranged in chronological order, typically without analysis or interpretation.

words.tr: n. （色彩、颜色、次序、音调等的）渐变；分等级；（各种状态、性质等的）分阶段渐变；元音交替
words.ex: The gradation of colors in the sunset is beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 日落时颜色的渐变很美。
words.en: A gradation is a series or a process in which things change into other things gradually and usually by very small stages.

words.ex: The clown entertains the children with funny tricks.
words.ex_cn: 小丑用滑稽的把戏娱乐孩子们。
words.en: To entertain someone means to amuse or interest them, for example by telling them stories or jokes, or by playing music for them.

words.tr: adj. 家庭的；国内的；驯养的；
words.ex: She prefers domestic chores over going out.
words.ex_cn: 她更喜欢做家务而不是外出。
words.en: Domestic means relating to the home, family, or household affairs. It can also refer to something that is made or produced within a country and not imported.

words.ex: He is an astute businessman who always makes smart decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他是个精明的商人，总是做出明智的决定。
words.en: If you describe someone as astute, you think they are clever and can see through things quickly and make good judgments.

words.tr: adj. 无法克服的；难以解决的；不可逾越的
words.ex: The problem seemed insurmountable.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题似乎无法克服。
words.en: If you describe something as insurmountable, you mean that it is so great or severe that it cannot be dealt with.

words.tr:
v. 奉承；讨好
adj. 更平坦的；更扁平的；“flat”的比较级
adv. 更平直地；更直截了当地；“flat”的比较级
words.ex: He flatters his boss to get a raise.
words.ex_cn: 他奉承老板以获得加薪。
words.en: If someone flatters you, they praise you in an exaggerated way that may be sincere or may be intended to persuade you to do something.

words.ex: It was sheer luck that he won the game.
words.ex_cn: 他赢了比赛完全是运气。
words.en: Sheer is used to emphasize that a state or situation is complete and does not involve or is not mixed with anything else.

words.tr: adj.  快活的；愉快的；高兴的
words.ex: His jovial nature made him popular among his colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他天性快活，这使他在同事中很受欢迎。
words.en: If you describe someone as jovial, you mean that they are happy and cheerful.

words.ex: He did a preliminary test before the main experiment.
words.ex_cn: 他在主要实验之前做了一个初步测试。
words.en: Preliminary means something that is done or happens before the main part or event, especially as an introduction or preparation.

words.ex: The authoritarian leader controls everything.
words.ex_cn: 这位专制的领导人控制一切。
words.en: An authoritarian government or leader has complete power and control over the people and does not allow political opposition.

words.tr: adj. 肥沃的；有繁殖力的；多产的；富饶的；
words.ex: The fertile land grows many crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片肥沃的土地长满了各种作物。
words.en: Land or soil that is fertile is able to support the growth of a large number of strong healthy plants.

words.ex: They tried to coerce him into signing the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图强迫他签署那份文件。
words.en: If you coerce someone into doing something, you make them do it, even though they do not want to.

words.tr:
n. 特征；报刊特写；
v. 以…为特色；是…的重要组成；
words.ex: The main feature of this phone is its long battery life.
words.ex_cn: 这款手机的主要特征是续航时间长。
words.en: A feature of something is an interesting or important part or characteristic of it.

words.ex: A quiet room is conducive to studying.
words.ex_cn: 安静的房间有助于学习。
words.en: If one thing is conducive to another thing, it makes the other thing likely to happen.

words.ex: She showed empathy when her friend cried.
words.ex_cn: 当她的朋友哭泣时，她表现出了同感。
words.en: The ability to understand and share the feelings of another.

words.ex: The government decided to codify the old laws.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定将旧法律编纂成典。
words.en: To codify means to arrange laws, rules, etc. into a systematic code.

words.ex: He compiles data from many surveys.
words.ex_cn: 他汇编来自许多调查的数据。
words.en: To compile means to collect information from different places and arrange it in a book, report, or list.

words.ex: He ate a moderate amount of food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了适量的食物。
words.en: If you moderate something or if it moderates, it becomes less extreme or violent, or if you moderate a discussion, you help the people in it to reach an agreement.

words.ex: He tried to counterfeit money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图伪造货币。
words.en: Made in exact imitation of something valuable with the intention to deceive or defraud.

words.ex: The epidemic spread quickly across the country.
words.ex_cn: 这种流行病迅速蔓延到全国。
words.en: An epidemic is a large number of cases of an infectious disease occurring at the same time.

words.tr:
adj. 疏远的；冷淡的
adv. 远离地
words.ex: He stayed aloof during the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上保持冷淡。
words.en: Someone who is aloof is not very friendly and does not like to spend time with other people.

words.ex: The police discovered a scheme to steal money.
words.ex_cn: 警方发现了一个偷钱的阴谋。
words.en: A scheme is a plan or arrangement, especially one produced by a government or other organization, or a secret plan to do something, especially something illegal or dishonest.

words.ex: Don't meddle in my affairs.
words.ex_cn: 别插手我的事情。
words.en: To meddle means to interfere in something that is not one's concern.

words.tr: v. 把…置于背景中考虑
words.ex: It is important to contextualize historical events to understand their true significance.
words.ex_cn: 将历史事件置于上下文中理解，以了解其真正的意义，这一点非常重要。
words.en: To contextualize something means to consider it in relation to the situation in which it happens or exists.

words.ex: The Industrial Revolution was a new epoch in history.
words.ex_cn: 工业革命是历史上一个新时代。
words.en: An epoch is a period of time in history or a person's life, typically one marked by notable events or particular characteristics.

words.ex: The storm deprived us of electricity.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴剥夺了我们的电力。
words.en: If you deprive someone of something that they want or need, you take it away from them, or you prevent them from having it.

words.ex: The ship carries a provision of food for the journey.
words.ex_cn: 这艘船为旅程准备了食物供应。
words.en: A provision is a condition or requirement in a legal document. It can also refer to the act of supplying or providing something that is needed.

words.tr:
v. 假定；要求
n. 假定；假设
words.ex: He postulates that all humans are equal.
words.ex_cn: 他假定所有人都是平等的。
words.en: If you postulate something, you suggest it as the basis for a theory, argument, or calculation.

words.tr:
adj. 奢侈的；慷慨给予的；挥霍的；过多的
v. 浪费；挥霍；慷慨给予
words.ex: He threw a lavish party for his birthday.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的生日举办了一场奢华的派对。
words.en: If you describe something as lavish, you mean that it is very elaborate and impressive and a lot of money has been spent on it. If you say that someone is lavish in the way they behave, you mean that they give, spend, or use a lot of something.

words.tr: v. 压制；平息；消除；减轻
words.ex: The police tried to quell the riot.
words.ex_cn: 警察试图平息暴乱。
words.en: To quell something, especially a feeling, means to stop it or reduce its intensity.

words.ex: The contract stipulates that payments must be made monthly.
words.ex_cn: 合同规定付款必须按月进行。
words.en: If you stipulate a condition or stipulate that something must be done, you say clearly that it must be done.

words.ex: The grandeur of the palace amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 宫殿的宏伟让每个人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The quality of being grand or splendid in appearance or style.

words.tr: n. 警告；防止误解的说明；注意事项
words.ex: He gave me a warning, a caveat, before I signed the contract.
words.ex_cn: 我在签署合同之前，他给了我一个警告，一个注意事项。
words.en: A caveat is a warning of a specific limitation of something such as information or an agreement.

words.ex: The memory of the accident still haunts him.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故的记忆仍然长期困扰着他。
words.en: If something unpleasant haunts you, you keep thinking or worrying about it over a long period of time. A place that is haunted is believed to be visited regularly by a ghost.

words.ex: He is scrupulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他检查作业时一丝不苟。
words.en: If you are scrupulous, you are careful, thorough, and extremely attentive to details.

words.tr: adj. （言行）谨慎的；不显眼的；朴素的
words.ex: He was discreet about his personal life.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的私生活很低调。
words.en: If you are discreet, you are polite and careful in what you do or say, because you want to avoid embarrassing or offending someone.

words.ex: The unfair verdict caused public outrage.
words.ex_cn: 不公正的判决引发了公众的愤怒。
words.en: An outrage is an extremely strong reaction of anger, shock, or indignation.
