words.ex: The police caught the culprit who stole the bike.
words.ex_cn: 警察抓住了偷自行车的罪犯。
words.en: A culprit is someone who has done something wrong or illegal.

words.tr: adj. 患狂犬病的；狂暴的；疯狂的
words.ex: The rabid dog ran wildly through the street.
words.ex_cn: 那只狂犬在街上狂奔。
words.en: If you describe someone as rabid, you mean that they have very strong and unreasonable opinions or beliefs about a subject, especially in politics.

words.tr: n. 商机；理想的工作或生活；
words.ex: He found a niche in selling eco-friendly phone cases.
words.ex_cn: 他在销售环保手机壳方面找到了商机。
words.en: A niche is a hollow area in a wall which has been made to hold a statue, or a comfortable or suitable position in life or employment.

words.tr: n. 避难所；庇护所；庇护；
words.ex: The birds found sanctuary in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这些鸟在森林里找到了避难所。
words.en: A sanctuary is a place where people or animals are protected from danger or trouble.

words.ex: The decision was consequential for the future of the company.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定对公司未来意义重大。
words.en: Something that is consequential is important or significant, often because it has effects on other things.

words.ex: This coupon is valid until next month.
words.ex_cn: 这张优惠券到下个月都有效。
words.en: If something such as a document or agreement is valid, it is legally acceptable or officially recognized.

words.ex: The earthquake was a terrible calamity.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场巨大的灾难。
words.en: A calamity is an event that causes great harm or damage, such as a flood or a fire.

words.tr:
n. 忧愁
adj.  忧郁的
words.ex: He felt melancholy after the rain stopped.
words.ex_cn: 雨停后，他感到忧郁。
words.en: A feeling of deep sadness, typically with no obvious cause.

words.ex: He gave a witty answer to the teacher's question.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师的问题给出了机智的回答。
words.en: Someone or something that is witty is amusing in a clever way.

words.ex: Her hug gave me solace after the loss.
words.ex_cn: 在失去亲人后，她的拥抱给了我安慰。
words.en: Solace is comfort that you feel when you are consoled in times of disappointment or sadness.

words.ex: The inquisitive child asked many questions about the stars.
words.ex_cn: 这个好奇的孩子问了很多关于星星的问题。
words.en: If you describe someone as inquisitive, you mean that they are interested in a lot of different things and want to find out more about them.

words.ex: The two teams showed synergy when they finished the project early.
words.ex_cn: 当这两个团队提前完成项目时，展现了协同效应。
words.en: The interaction or cooperation of two or more organizations, substances, or other agents to produce a combined effect greater than the sum of their separate effects.

words.ex: He feels comfortable in his artistic milieu.
words.ex_cn: 他在他的艺术环境中感到自在。
words.en: The milieu is the environment or setting in which something happens or develops.

words.ex: He has a propensity for telling the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他有说实话的倾向。
words.en: A propensity is a natural tendency to behave in a particular way.

words.tr:
adj. 精心制作的；详尽的；
v. 精心制作；详尽阐述；
words.ex: She wore an elaborate dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件精心制作的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: To elaborate means to add more details to something that has already been said or written, making it more complex or detailed. As an adjective, it describes something that is very complex and detailed.

words.tr:
v. 畏缩不前；犹豫；妨碍
n. 阻碍，妨碍
words.ex: He balks at paying high prices.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意支付高价。
words.en: If you balk at something, you hesitate to do it or agree to it, often because it is unpleasant or difficult.

words.ex: The advent of smartphones changed how we communicate.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机的到来改变了我们的交流方式。
words.en: The arrival of a notable person, thing, or event.

words.ex: The abolition of slavery took many years.
words.ex_cn: 废除奴隶制花了许多年。
words.en: The act of officially ending or stopping something, such as a system, practice, or institution.

words.tr:
n. 尖塔；尖顶；尖峰；尖岩石；顶点；顶峰
v. 造小尖塔；把...放在极高处
words.ex: The pinnacle of the church reached high into the sky.
words.ex_cn: 教堂的尖塔高耸入云。
words.en: The pinnacle of something is the highest point or level that it can reach, especially when it is very good.

words.ex: The teacher underscored the importance of homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师强调了作业的重要性。
words.en: To emphasize the importance of something or to draw a line underneath a word or phrase.

words.tr:
v. 聚成块；聚成堆；凝聚
adj. 成团的；结块的；聚结的
n. 团块；凝聚物；集块岩
words.ex: The dust particles tend to agglomerate in the presence of moisture.
words.ex_cn: 在有湿气的情况下，灰尘颗粒往往会结块。
words.en: To agglomerate means to gather into a cluster or mass, or to cause to gather into such a cluster or mass. As a noun, it refers to a mass or collection of things; a cluster.

words.tr: adj. 在职的；负有义务的；
words.ex: The incumbent mayor won the election again.
words.ex_cn: 现任市长再次赢得了选举。
words.en: An incumbent is someone who currently holds a particular office or position, especially in politics. It can also refer to something that is necessary as a duty or responsibility.

words.ex: The doctor checked his gut for signs of infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了他的肠道是否有感染迹象。
words.en: The gut refers to the stomach and other internal organs of an animal or person, often used to describe the digestive tract. It can also metaphorically represent courage or determination.

words.ex: He had no wherewith to buy food.
words.ex_cn: 他没有钱买食物。
words.en: The means or resources with which to do something.

words.tr: n. 不适当；不正确；不得体
words.ex: His impropriety at the meeting shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上的不恰当行为让所有人都感到震惊。
words.en: Impropriety is the quality or state of being improper, especially in behavior or speech.

words.ex: I presume he will arrive tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我假设他明天会到。
words.en: If you presume that something is the case, you think that it is the case, although you are not certain.

words.ex: The government does a census every ten years.
words.ex_cn: 政府每十年进行一次人口普查。
words.en: A census is an official count or survey of a population, typically recording various details of individuals.

words.tr: v. 布置家具；配备；供给；提供
words.ex: He will furnish the apartment with new furniture.
words.ex_cn: 他将为公寓配备新家具。
words.en: To furnish a place means to put furniture and other things into it.

words.tr: n. 绝境；僵局；死路；死胡同
words.ex: The talks reached an impasse and no one could move forward.
words.ex_cn: 谈判陷入了僵局，没有人能继续前进。
words.en: An impasse is a situation in which no progress can be made or no advancement is possible, especially because of disagreement; a deadlock.

words.tr:
v. 叛乱；反叛；（使）厌恶
n. 叛乱；厌恶；反感
words.ex: The people revolt against the unfair rules.
words.ex_cn: 人们反抗不公平的规则。
words.en: If a large number of people revolt, they refuse to be controlled or ruled, and take action against authority, often violent action.

words.ex: He infringes the rules by arriving late.
words.ex_cn: 他因迟到而违反了规则。
words.en: To infringe means to violate or break a law, agreement, or right.

words.ex: The judge made an equitable decision.
words.ex_cn: 法官做出了一个公平的决定。
words.en: Fair and impartial; treating everyone equally.

words.tr: adj. 谦逊的；不夸耀的；不矫饰的
words.ex: The house had an unpretentious charm that made it feel welcoming.
words.ex_cn: 这座房子有一种不炫耀的魅力，让人感到宾至如归。
words.en: If you describe a place, person, or thing as unpretentious, you approve of them because they are simple in appearance or character, rather than sophisticated or luxurious.

words.ex: He is adept at solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长解决数学问题。
words.en: Someone who is adept at something is very skilled at it.

words.tr: v. 使减细；使减小；使减弱
words.ex: The wire attenuates as it gets longer.
words.ex_cn: 这根电线随着变长而变细。
words.en: To reduce the force, effect, or value of something.

words.tr: v. 激怒；使急躁；使疼痛
words.ex: Loud noises irritate my baby.
words.ex_cn: 噪音会激怒我的宝宝。
words.en: If something irritates you, it keeps annoying you.

words.tr:
v. 发牢骚；抱怨；轰鸣
n. 怨言；牢骚；轰隆声
words.ex: He grumbles when he has to wake up early.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不早起时就会抱怨。
words.en: If someone grumbles, they complain about something in a bad-tempered way.

words.ex: The new law gave impetus to environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 新法律为环境保护提供了推动力。
words.en: Something that gives a process impetus or an impetus makes it happen or progress more quickly.

words.ex: There was a surge in sales during the holiday season.
words.ex_cn: 假期期间销量激增。
words.en: If something surges, it increases suddenly and greatly, after having been steady or only small in size or amount.

words.tr: n. 民间传说；民俗学；民间风俗；
words.ex: The old man told us a folklore about a dragon living in the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 老人给我们讲了一个关于住在山里的龙的民间传说。
words.en: Folklore is the traditional stories, customs, and habits of a particular community or nation.

words.ex: He gave a concise answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了简明的回答。
words.en: Something that is concise says everything that is necessary without using any unnecessary words.

words.ex: He showed forbearance when his friend made a mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当他的朋友犯错时，他表现出了忍耐。
words.en: Forbearance is the quality of being patient and being able to control your temper in difficult situations.

words.ex: He was wary of strangers who offered free gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他对那些提供免费礼物的陌生人保持谨慎。
words.en: If you are wary of something or someone, you are cautious because you do not know much about them and you believe they may be dangerous or cause problems.

words.ex: The school has stringent rules about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学校对作业有严格的规定。
words.en: Stringent measures, rules, or conditions are very strict or severe.

words.tr:
n. 亡命之徒；逃犯；被剥夺法律权益者
v. 宣布…为非法；使…成为非法
words.ex: The police caught the outlaw last night.
words.ex_cn: 警察昨晚抓住了那个不法之徒。
words.en: An outlaw is a person who has broken the law and who is hiding or running away to avoid punishment. To outlaw something means to make it illegal.

words.tr: adj. 全神贯注的； v. “preoccupy”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He was preoccupied with his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他全神贯注于他的作业。
words.en: If you are preoccupied, you are thinking a lot about something or someone, and so you hardly notice other things.

words.ex: The city had an economic boom after the new factory opened.
words.ex_cn: 新工厂开业后，这座城市迎来了经济繁荣。
words.en: If there is a boom in the economy, there is an increase in economic activity, for example in the amount of things that are being bought and sold.

words.tr:
v. 潜伏；隐藏
n. 潜伏；埋伏
words.ex: A cat lurks behind the bush.
words.ex_cn: 一只猫躲在灌木丛后。
words.en: To lurk means to wait or move in a secretive way so that you cannot be seen, especially because you are about to attack someone or do something wrong.

words.tr: v. 割让（领土）；放弃（权力）
words.ex: He will cede his land to the government.
words.ex_cn: 他将把土地让给政府。
words.en: To give up control or possession of something, especially land or territory, often as a result of war or negotiation.

words.ex: The vase remained intact after the fall.
words.ex_cn: 花瓶从高处摔下后依然完整无缺。
words.en: Something that is intact is complete and has not been damaged or changed.

words.ex: The imperious queen demanded immediate obedience.
words.ex_cn: 这位专横的女王要求立即服从。
words.en: If you describe someone as imperious, you mean that they have a proud manner and expect to be obeyed.

words.tr: n. 漠不关心；无动于衷
words.ex: He showed nonchalance when the glass fell.
words.ex_cn: 当玻璃杯掉下来时，他表现得若无其事。
words.en: The state of being nonchalant; a casual lack of concern or indifference.

words.ex: The teacher commends her for working hard.
words.ex_cn: 老师表扬她学习努力。
words.en: If you commend someone or something, you praise them formally.

words.ex: The temporal change of seasons affects our daily life.
words.ex_cn: 季节的时间变化影响我们的日常生活。
words.en: Relating to time as opposed to eternity; relating to worldly life as opposed to spiritual life.

words.tr: n. 祸根；致命伤；烦扰之源；
words.ex: Smoking is the bane of his health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟是他健康的祸根。
words.en: Something that causes misery or death.

words.ex: He delves into the history of ancient civilizations.
words.ex_cn: 他探究古代文明的历史。
words.en: If you delve into something, you try to discover new information about it by searching or investigating carefully.

words.tr: adj. 无可挑剔的；无瑕疵的；
words.ex: Her impeccable manners impressed everyone at the dinner.
words.ex_cn: 她无可挑剔的礼仪让晚宴上的每个人都印象深刻。
words.en: If you describe something as impeccable, you are emphasizing that it is perfect and has no faults.

words.tr:
v. 阻挠；妨碍；挫败
n. 横坐板
words.ex: The rain thwarted our picnic plans.
words.ex_cn: 雨水破坏了我们的野餐计划。
words.en: If you thwart someone or thwart their plans, you prevent them from doing or getting what they want.

words.ex: It is the president's prerogative to make final decisions.
words.ex_cn: 做最终决定是总统的特权。
words.en: A prerogative is a right or privilege exclusive to a particular individual or class.

words.ex: The box contains five apples.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子包含五个苹果。
words.en: If something such as a box, bag, room, or place contains things, those things are inside it.

words.tr: adj. 不留心的；不注意的
words.ex: He was heedless of the warning signs.
words.ex_cn: 他对警告信号毫不在意。
words.en: If you are heedless of someone or something, you do not take any notice of them.

words.ex: He attests that the document is true.
words.ex_cn: 他证明这份文件是真实的。
words.en: To attest something means to declare or affirm that it is true or genuine, often in a formal or legal context.

words.ex: He tried to curb his horse with the reins.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用缰绳勒住马。
words.en: If you curb something, you control it and keep it within limits.

words.ex: I met him at a party, but he is only an acquaintance.
words.ex_cn: 我在聚会上认识了他，但他只是个熟人。
words.en: An acquaintance is someone you know a little, who is not a close friend.

words.ex: The cat creeps slowly toward the bird.
words.ex_cn: 猫蹑手蹑脚地向鸟靠近。
words.en: To move slowly and quietly, especially in a way that does not attract attention.

words.tr:
v. 痛哭；嚎啕；尖叫
n. 痛哭；哀号；尖啸
words.ex: The baby wails when she is hungry.
words.ex_cn: 当宝宝饿的时候，她会哭喊。
words.en: To wail means to make a long, high cry, usually because you are in pain or very sad.

words.ex: The government imposed a new tax on sugar.
words.ex_cn: 政府对糖征收了一项新税。
words.en: To impose means to officially force a rule, tax, punishment, etc. to be obeyed or received.

words.tr:
n. 硬币；金属钱币；
v. 创造；
words.ex: He has a coin in his pocket.
words.ex_cn: 他口袋里有一枚硬币。
words.en: A coin is a small, flat, round piece of metal or plastic that is used as money.

words.tr: adj. 热烈的；强烈的；热情的
words.ex: He is a fervent supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心支持者。
words.en: having or showing very strong and sincere feelings about something

words.ex: He made a pledge to help the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了帮助穷人的保证。
words.en: A pledge is a serious promise or agreement, especially one made publicly or officially. It can also refer to something given as security for the fulfillment of a contract or the payment of a debt.

words.ex: Her husband cooks dinner every night.
words.ex_cn: 她的丈夫每天晚上做晚饭。
words.en: A married man considered in relation to his spouse.

words.ex: The two countries signed a protocol to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了一项停止战争的协议。
words.en: A protocol is a set of rules or a system of rules about the correct way to act in formal situations.

words.tr:
adj. 无数的；
n. 无数；
words.ex: There are myriad stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有无数的星星。
words.en: A myriad of things or people is a very large number of them.

words.tr:
n. 吸引力；上诉；
v. 吸引；诉请；呼吁；
words.ex: The appeal of the beach drew many tourists.
words.ex_cn: 海滩的吸引力吸引了许多游客。
words.en: If you appeal to someone to do something, you make a serious and urgent request to them. If you appeal against a decision or sentence, you formally ask a court or other authority to change it. If something appeals to you, you like it or it interests you.

words.tr:
n. 闪耀；闪烁；小发光物
v. 闪耀；闪亮；流露（感情）
words.ex: The glitter of the stars lit up the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 星星的闪耀照亮了夜空。
words.en: If something glitters, light comes from or is reflected off different parts of it.

words.ex: His joke brought some levity to the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话为会议带来了一些轻松气氛。
words.en: Levity refers to a lack of seriousness, especially at an inappropriate time, often characterized by frivolity or lightness of manner.

words.ex: His discourse on climate change was clear and logical.
words.ex_cn: 他关于气候变化的论述清晰而有逻辑。
words.en: Discourse is spoken or written communication between people, especially serious discussion of a particular subject.

words.ex: He gave a spiteful look when he lost the game.
words.ex_cn: 他输掉比赛时投来一个恶毒的眼神。
words.en: If you say that someone is spiteful, you mean that they deliberately want to upset or hurt someone, often in a small way, because they feel angry towards them.

words.ex: The governor signed the new law yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 州长昨天签署了这项新法律。
words.en: A governor is a person who is responsible for the political administration of a region, such as a state or a colony.

words.ex: The roof has a sharp slant.
words.ex_cn: 屋顶有一个陡峭的倾斜。
words.en: If something slants or if you slant it, it is at an angle rather than being straight up and down or straight from side to side.

words.tr: n. 陷阱；隐患；想不到的困难；
words.ex: Don't ignore the pitfall of skipping homework.
words.ex_cn: 不要忽视不做作业这个陷阱。
words.en: A pitfall is a likely mistake or problem in a situation.

words.ex: The coach changed his tactic to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 教练改变了战术以赢得比赛。
words.en: A tactic is a method or plan chosen to bring about a desired future, such as achieving a goal or solving a problem.

words.tr: adj. 有害的；恶性的；致命的
words.ex: Smoking is a pernicious habit.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟是一种有害的习惯。
words.en: Having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way.

words.tr: v. 使着迷；使陶醉；对…施魔法
words.ex: The magic show enchants the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演让孩子们着迷。
words.en: If you are enchanted by someone or something, they cause you to have feelings of great delight or pleasure.

words.ex: He gave a scornful look when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 当她说话时，他投去轻蔑的一眼。
words.en: If you are scornful of someone or something, you show contempt or disdain for them.

words.tr: adj. 扭歪的；啼笑皆非的；挖苦的；讽刺的
words.ex: He gave a wry smile when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到这个消息时露出了苦笑。
words.en: If someone has a wry expression, it shows that they find a bad situation or a change in a situation slightly amusing.

words.tr:
v. 闪烁；隐约闪现
n. 亮光；闪光
words.ex: The sun gleams on the water.
words.ex_cn: 阳光照在水面上，闪闪发亮。
words.en: A gleam is a small, bright light, especially one that shines for a short time.

words.tr:
n. 没收物；罚金
v. 丧失；被没收
words.ex: He had to pay a forfeit for breaking the rule.
words.ex_cn: 他因违反规定不得不支付没收物。
words.en: If you forfeit something, you lose it or are forced to give it up because you have broken a rule or done something wrong.

words.tr: adj. 机会主义的；投机取巧的
words.ex: He is opportunistic and always takes advantage of easy chances.
words.ex_cn: 他很 opportunistic，总是抓住容易的机会。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as opportunistic, you are critical of them because they take advantage of situations in order to gain money or power, without thinking about whether their actions are right or wrong.

words.ex: The rubber band is elastic.
words.ex_cn: 橡皮筋是有弹性的。
words.en: An elastic material is able to stretch and then return to its original shape or size.

words.ex: The university conferred an honorary degree on him.
words.ex_cn: 大学授予他一个荣誉学位。
words.en: To confer something such as a degree or an honor on someone means to give it to them in a formal way. To confer with someone means to discuss something with them in order to make a decision.

words.tr:
n. 诉讼当事人
adj. 有关诉讼的
words.ex: The litigant spoke clearly in court.
words.ex_cn: 这位诉讼当事人在法庭上清晰地发言。
words.en: A litigant is a person who is involved in a lawsuit.

words.ex: The movie is a satire about politicians.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是一部关于政治家的讽刺作品。
words.en: A way of criticizing people or ideas in a humorous way, especially in order to make a political point, or a piece of writing that uses this style.

words.tr: v. 给予选举权；释放（奴隶）
words.ex: The law will enfranchise all adults over 18.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律将赋予所有18岁以上成年人选举权。
words.en: To enfranchise someone means to give them the right to vote in elections.

words.ex: The river water looked murky after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后，河水看起来污浊。
words.en: If you describe something as murky, you mean that the details of it are not clear or that it is difficult to understand.

words.ex: His calm demeanor made everyone feel safe.
words.ex_cn: 他平静的举止让每个人都感到安心。
words.en: The way in which a person behaves towards others; outward behavior or bearing.

words.tr: adj. 著名的； v. 庆祝；“celebrate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is a celebrated painter in China.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位在中国著名的画家。
words.en: A celebrated person or thing is famous and much admired.

words.ex: The children were boisterous at the party.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在聚会上喧闹不已。
words.en: Someone who is boisterous is noisy, lively, and full of energy.

words.tr:
n. 分钟；一会儿；
adj. 微小的；极小的；
words.ex: I waited for five minutes.
words.ex_cn: 我等了五分钟。
words.en: A minute is a unit of time equal to sixty seconds or a sixtieth of an hour.

words.ex: He is a man of great eminence in science.
words.ex_cn: 他在科学界享有很高的声望。
words.en: Eminence refers to a position of great distinction or superiority, especially in a particular field or profession.
